criteria.await_drain: Each send holds for drain or free buffer room until the caller deadline lapses instead of failing on a full queue.
criteria.drain_event: Drain resumes queued server sends as its own session event; clients fail fast because their API offers no drain signal.
criteria.fail_fast: Full queues fail the send immediately with a domain error, whether native said -1 or the client buffer hit its cap.

backpressure.instructions: What should a send do when the queue is full?

criteria.callback: Connect and accept take checked callbacks that fire per event and carry grouped session state.
criteria.reader: Inbound events flow through a stream::reader of ws::event vended at connect and accept, sharing stream close and cancel, with sends staying on the session.
criteria.receive: Sessions stay one opaque value: ws::receive draws a ws::event variant per pull and the same value takes send and close.

surface.instructions: How do session events reach Can code?

criteria.explicit_insecure: Callers may name insecurity explicitly for loopback and self-signed peers; verification stays the default.
criteria.no_wss: Wss URLs are refused outright and only ws:// connects, leaving TLS termination beyond Can.
criteria.verify_only: OS trust verifies each wss handshake unconditionally, so self-signed peers can only fail.

tls_client.instructions: What TLS choice does the client offer?

criteria.accept_op: A handler upgrades its own request through ws::accept; the adapter finds the stored native request and server, and dispatch then withholds the HTTP reply.
criteria.marked_route: Marked routes upgrade inside dispatch before the handler runs, so the handler meets a session rather than a request.
criteria.separate_serve: WebSockets serve through a dedicated ws::serve and Bun.serve pair, decoupled from the HTTP router.
